# Hook lean

**After the context, what makes the viewer want the next sentence?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C12


## Proof: a stat, screenshot or result
<a id="proof"></a>

Back the context at once with a number, screenshot or visible result.

**Looks like:** Context line, then a retention graph, a GitHub star count ticking up, or the plate count on the bar. The viewer sees it is real before the explanation.

**Good at:** trust; falsifiable, so believable; pairs with counters

**Weak at:** needs real data; dry numbers without a story feel flat

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short, carousel · niches all · goals trust, retention · effort low

**How:** Screenshot or screen-record the proof. Add a number counter (HyperFrames or CapCut keyframes) and a highlight on the key line.

**Backed by:** [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Point, don't talk; give me a fact](../topics/text.md#text-point-dont-talk), [Show proof on screen](../topics/editing.md#edit-proof-inserts), [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L01, L09, R1

## Pain point or benefit
<a id="pain-or-benefit"></a>

Name a specific struggle the viewer has, or the outcome they want.

**Looks like:** 'Your Claude edits look pro but sound like a silent movie.' Or '...without paying for Photoshop.' The line makes the viewer feel the problem is theirs.

**Good at:** relatability; saves; clear audience targeting

**Weak at:** generic pains sound like ads; needs to be specific to land

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals saves, retention · effort low

**How:** Write the pain in the viewer's own words, taken from comments or Reddit. A caption pop is enough.

**Backed by:** [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Question on a pain point](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pain-question), [Ideas from DM and comment questions](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-questions-not-polls), [Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L01, L02, L05, L11

## Shocking or unexpected fact
<a id="shock-fact"></a>

An unexpected image, statement or fact. L01 counts it as a valid lean; Caleb calls it 'getting a little tiresome'.

**Looks like:** Context line, then 'Your 2FA code works with Wi-Fi off.' The phone in airplane mode keeps changing the code on screen. A surprise that makes the viewer stay to learn why.

**Good at:** thumb stop; shares ('did you know'); fast to write

**Weak at:** audiences are tiring of it (L05); feels clickbait if the fact is weak

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short · niches all · goals reach, shares · effort low

**How:** One line plus a visual proof of the fact. B&W freeze or punch-in on the reveal.

**Backed by:** [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Unexpected-fact hooks are wearing thin](../topics/hooks.md#hook-unexpected-facts-tiresome), ["Do this now": a tiny effort, instant payoff](../topics/hooks.md#hook-do-this-now), [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula), [Statement, reason, re-hook, "Why?", payoff](../topics/story.md#story-live-hook-build) · sources L01, L05, R1

## Bold contrarian statement
<a id="contrarian-statement"></a>

Lean with a belief that goes against the crowd. Caleb prefers this over unexpected facts.

**Looks like:** Context: 'Gym progress.' Lean: 'Your program doesn't matter as much as you think.' The viewer stays to see if you can defend it.

**Good at:** comments; positioning; memorable

**Weak at:** must be defended in the body; can alienate if it's just provocation

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches all · goals comments, trust · effort low

**How:** Say it to camera with a punch-in. Use the '8 Mile' structure in the body to answer the obvious objection.

**Backed by:** [Unexpected-fact hooks are wearing thin](../topics/hooks.md#hook-unexpected-facts-tiresome), [Contrarian statement or "don't buy X"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrarian-statement), ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile), [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula) · sources L05, L06

## Odd pattern interrupt
<a id="pattern-interrupt"></a>

Something strange in the frame or the line that breaks the scroll before it makes sense.

**Looks like:** 'I eat blueberries like it's my job... you missed the first 30.' Or an odd object planted in frame that people will comment about. The weirdness is the lean.

**Good at:** thumb stop; comments ('why is there a...'); personality

**Weak at:** can confuse; the topic still has to arrive fast

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short, story · niches all · goals reach, comments · effort low

**How:** Plan the odd detail in the shot list, or open on the oddest frame you filmed.

**Backed by:** [Pattern-interrupt opener](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pattern-interrupt), [Comment farm: plant an odd detail](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-comment-farm), [Voice cadence as pattern interrupt](../topics/sound.md#sound-voice-cadence-interrupt), [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula), [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways) · sources L05, L08

## Mixing
Proof plus contrarian is the strongest pairing (a bold line backed at once). Pain plus proof is the classic tutorial lean.

## Rule of thumb
Trust and saves: proof or pain. Comments: contrarian or pattern interrupt. Reach with a fresh fact: shock fact, used sparingly.
